title: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler ITDR

blocks.text: This guide takes you through the configuration steps that you need to complete to begin using Zscaler ITDR for your organization.
Before you begin configuring ITDR, Zscaler recommends reading the What Is Zscaler ITDR? article.
To configure ITDR, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: Step 1: Log In to the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal
After your organization is provisioned for ITDR, you will receive an email with the following details:
Link to your ITDR instance
Link to set your password
Security code
Click the password link to set your password and the two-factor authentication (2FA) code. To learn more, see Accessing and Navigating the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
Step 2: Configure Users and Roles
Zscaler recommends that you use the Authentication Service Admin Portal to add users and roles. Contact Zscaler Support to subscribe to Authentication Service.
You can provision users who can access the ITDR Admin Portal. Users can access and manage different modules in the portal based on the roles assigned to them. To learn more, see About Users & Roles.
Step 3: Configure Single Sign-On Authentication

Zscaler recommends that you use the Authentication Service Admin Portal to configure primary and secondary external identity providers (IdPs). Authentication Service supports both SAML and OpenID configurations.
You can enable single sign-on (SSO) to your ITDR Admin Portal via SAML or OpenID. To learn more, see the following articles:

Step 4: Configure Threat Detection Policies
You can create a threat detection policy and specify a selection criterion to apply to an endpoint for real-time threat detection. To learn more, see the following articles:
About Threat Detection Policies
Creating Threat Detection Policies
Evaluating Threat Detection Policies
Specifying Selection Criterion for Threat Detection Policies

Step 5: Integrate ITDR with Okta
You can integrate ITDR with Okta to enrich the identity metadata, identify real-time changes, and perform actions on an Okta identity. To learn more, see the following articles:
Integrating ITDR with Okta
Viewing Active Directory User Account Details
Step 6: Assess Your Active Directory Posture
You can add an Active Directory (AD) domain and assign an endpoint agent to scan the AD domain for identity misconfigurations. To learn more, see the following articles:
About Active Directory Posture Scan
Scanning an Active Directory
Managing Active Directory Attribute Collection Settings
Triggering an On-Demand Scan for Active Directory
Step 7: Assess Your Entra ID Posture

You can connect your organization's Entra ID tenants with ITDR to identify misconfigurations and potential risks across Entra ID users, service principals, and roles. To learn more, see the following articles:
About Entra ID Posture Scan
Connecting an Entra ID Tenant with the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal

Triggering an On-Demand Scan for an Entra ID Tenant
Step 8: Set Up Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan
You can scan endpoints to identify exposed credentials and disrupt lateral movements. To learn more, see the following articles:
About Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan

Step 10: Enable Change Detection

You can monitor and detect active changes in an AD domain and Entra ID tenant and classify these changes as a good or bad impact. In addition to the default changes, you can configure custom policies to detect changes. To learn more, see the following articles:

You can remediate risky AD and Entra ID identities and bad changes directly from the ITDR Admin Portal. Remediating risky identities improves the security posture of your identity infrastructure. To learn more, see the following articles:
